entries.subject: DAMIT 1873: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-1873.txt. Model 1873, version 2018-03-22, pole (95°, 19°), period 26.4614 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 107 ±5 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Marciniak et al. (2018), Photometric survey, modelling, and scaling of long-period and low-amplitude asteroids
entries.finding: [Marciniak et al. (2018), Photometric survey, modelling, and scaling of long-period and low-amplitude asteroids](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A%26A...610A...7M) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 95.61 ± 1.56 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 227 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Marciniak et al. (2018), A&A 610, A7
entries.finding: [Marciniak et al. (2018), A&A 610, A7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.01893) — retained primary publication; see the body-specific selection and calibration above.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 1874, pole ['272', '-1'], [Model 1874](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/1874) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 1874: pole (272°, -1°), 26.4613 h, version 2018-03-22, archive diameter 108 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: Shown size Display reference radius "50.5 km (size-calibrated model)" (marciniak-2018-slow-asteroids) differs from the NEOWISE V2.0 neowise_mainbelt.csv record 182 (Masiero et al. 2014) diameter 94.635 ± 2.556 km (NEOWISE, NEATM); the shown value is kept.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.

entries.subject: Philosophia whole-disc color
entries.finding: Gaia Collaboration, Galluccio et al. (2023) published the mean of 38 Gaia epoch spectra of the unresolved disc: reflectance against the Sun in 16 bands from 374 to 1034 nm, 1 at 550 nm (0.926 at 462 nm, 0.982 at 638 nm). The shape is painted in that one color (#484845 in sRGB) through the shared disc-integrated-color method, scaled to the 6.5% geometric albedo JPL lists (± 0.4%), from NEOWISE (Masiero et al. 2014, ApJ 791, 121; PDS bundle neowise_diameters_albedos 2.0). It is one mean, not a map. Tinaut-Ruano et al. (2023), A&A 669, L14, found Gaia DR3 reflectances slightly too red at wavelengths shorter than 550 nm; the bands are used as published, without that paper's correction.
